title: Cloud marketplace partnership checklist & listing copy (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is a working draft for marketplace listings and partner/go-to-market requirements for AWS, Azure, and GCP. It contains draft marketing copy variations, a technical and commercial checklist for legal/compliance/procurement, and the operational tasks required to publish Redwood Inference in each cloud marketplace and support private/offered procurement (private offers, BYOL, or SaaS subscription).

Status notes / how to use this doc
- Status: in_review — please add comments inline or drop notes in #gtm-marketplace Slack.
- Owners: Jordan (listing copy + AWS), Asha (azure path + legal), Mateo (GCP + billing), Priya (screens + assets), Samir (partner ops and launch gating).
- Target launch cadence: staggered pilot on AWS first (Q1 FY26), followed by Azure, then GCP.
- Key open questions (TODO): private offer pricing model, whether to support marketplace metering vs. vendor-managed billing for Dedicated contracts, required SOC2 artifact bundle for Azure marketplace.

1) Short listing copy variants (for marketplace summary cards)
- Variant A (developer-first): "Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference: predictable latency, lower token cost, and enterprise deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private)."
- Variant B (SaaS procurement friendly): "Redwood Inference: Scalable, SLA-backed LLM inference with marketplace billing and enterprise-grade security."
- Variant C (technical/feature lead): "High-throughput GPU inference runtime with smart routing, KV caching, and simple API for text, chat, embeddings, and reranks."

2) Long description (marketing + technical) — single canonical text to adapt per marketplace
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform built for teams shipping LLM features at scale. Our runtime combines GPU-optimized serving, intelligent caching and batching, and model routing to deliver predictable latency and improved unit economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Use Redwood to: reduce inference cost through caching/quantization recommendations, maintain uptime with automatic fallbacks across model variants and regions, and operate securely with private control plane and KMS integrations for regulated workloads.

Core capabilities
- REST + SDKs for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Streaming, function/tool-calling, and structured outputs
- Dedicated GPU pools and reserved capacity for predictable throughput
- Private (VPC & on-prem) deployments with KMS/HSM integration
- Console: token-level cost breakdowns, model rollouts, A/B testing, and eval-triggered regression alerts

3) Feature bullets (for marketplace UI fields)
- Plug-and-play API: get started in minutes with quickstart templates
- Predictable latency SLOs and dedicated capacity options
- Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and quantization recommendations
- Compliance-ready: SOC2, audit logs, enterprise SSO & KMS
- Flexible billing: usage-based API, reserved capacity contracts, private offers

4) Technical integration checklist (minimum required artifacts)
- Artifact: OIDC/SAML integration details and SSO test account [owner: Asha] (status: TODO)
- Artifact: SOC2 Type II report (redacted) + summary page [owner: Samir] (status: request to security)
- Artifact: Public pricing matrix + SKU mapping for each marketplace SKU variant (usage, reserved, dedicated) [owner: Mateo] (status: draft)
- Artifact: AMI/container image or SaaS integration manifest depending on marketplace packaging (AWS AMI/ECS listing, Azure managed app, GCP marketplace SaaS listing) [owner: Mateo/ Priya] (status: in_progress)
- Artifact: License/terms snippet and support SLA to include in listing (7x24 vs business hours) [owner: Legal] (status: need_input)
- Artifact: Billing metering contract template if using marketplace metering APIs [owner: Finance + Mateo] (status: TODO)
- Artifact: Minimum required security checklist (VPC, private networking options, KMS, audit logs) [owner: Security] (status: requested)

5) Commercial / procurement checklist
- Decide allowed purchase flows: SaaS on marketplace (metering), private offer (PO), or resale via partner. Pros/cons table:
  - Marketplace metering: easier procurement, but revenue share and metering complexity.
  - Private offer: supports committed Dedicated contracts and discounts, better margin, requires commercial approvals and procurement templates.
  - Vendor-managed billing: simpler for large enterprise deals but needs billing reconciliation flow.
- SKU design: Map product SKUs to marketplace SKUs. Example SKUs: RWI-API-ONDEMAND, RWI-DED-1GPU-MONTH, RWI-PRIVATE-VPC-INFRA. [owner: Finance]
- Minimum pricing guidelines: list baseline per-token for hosted + reserved pricing tiers for Dedicated. [owner: Pricing] (status: draft)
- Support SLAs linked to SKU: specify included support level for marketplace purchases vs. reserved contracts. [owner: Support]

6) Marketing assets required
- 1 hero screenshot: Console model dashboard + token breakdown (PNG, 1200x628) [owner: Priya] (status: in_progress)
- 3 product screenshots (API quickstart, rollout/AB test UI, cost analysis) [owner: Priya] (status: TODO)
- 1 one-pager PDF for procurement with SOC2 bullet list and contract summary [owner: Jordan / Legal] (status: draft)
- Logo pack: transparent + dark bg variations (SVG/PNG) [owner: Brand] (status: ready)
- Short intro video (60s) — timeline TBD for first marketplace (optional)

7) Marketplace-specific considerations (notes + differences)
- AWS Marketplace
  - Packaging options: AMI (self-managed), SaaS listings (API-based), private offers, or AMI+SaaS hybrid.
  - Metering options: usage-based metering (metering APIs) or subscription. For hosted API we can use metering, but for Dedicated/reserved we should prefer private offers.
  - Required artifacts: listing manifest, product short/long description, logo, screenshots, support contact, procurement contract templates.
  - Timeline note: AWS listing review takes ~5–10 business days; private offers add legal review time.

- Azure Marketplace
  - Packaging: Managed Applications (ARM templates) vs SaaS. Azure has more prescriptive onboarding for private networks.
  - Compliance: Azure often asks for customer-facing SOC2 evidence and specific data residency commitments for private offers.
  - Commercial nuance: Azure sometimes prefers Microsoft-led procurement for enterprise customers.

- GCP Marketplace
  - Packaging: SaaS or VM images/containers (GCP Marketplace tends to push SaaS for hosted services).
  - Billing: Integrations for Google Cloud billing mostly straightforward for SaaS — confirm metering connector.
  - Notes: GCP requires distinct listing metadata and privacy policy links — prepare a marketplace-specific TOS snippet.

8) Launch gating checklist (pre-publication)
- [ ] Finalized short + long copy for each marketplace and localization if needed [owner: Jordan]
- [ ] Approved pricing SKUs and commercial terms including revenue share math [owner: Finance]
- [ ] Signed SOC2 artifact delivery or redacted report ready for posting [owner: Security]
- [ ] Technical integration tests: SSO, metering callbacks, provisioning (if managed app) [owner: Eng/Platform]
- [ ] Upload hero + screenshots + logos to marketplace portal [owner: Priya]
- [ ] Legal approves marketplace terms/CTS snippet [owner: Legal]
- [ ] Launch comms: GTM enablement deck + partner sales one-pager [owner: GTM]

9) Example listing copy block (ready-to-paste draft for AWS/Azure/GCP fields)
Short summary (50–150 chars):
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private).

Full description (ready block):
Redwood Inference makes it easy to run and scale LLM-powered features in production. Our GPU-optimized runtime supports modern attention optimizations, continuous batching, KV-cache caching, and quantization-friendly execution paths to deliver low-latency responses and lower per-token costs. Choose hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated capacity for predictability and isolation, or Private deployment for regulatory and data residency needs. The Redwood Console provides cost visibility, model rollouts, and automatic fallbacks to keep your service reliable. Integrates with SSO, KMS, and enterprise audit logging.

Key features (bullet list copy):
- Fast REST + SDKs for text, chat, and embeddings
- Dedicated GPU pools and reserved capacity options
- Intelligent batching and caching to reduce unit cost
- Audit logs, SSO, and KMS integrations for enterprise security

10) Launch timeline (proposed)
- Week 0–2: finalize copy, assets, and legal templates
- Week 2–4: implement/verify integration hooks (metering callbacks, SSO test account, provisioning templates)
- Week 4–6: internal compliance review, upload to marketplace portal, submit for listing review
- Week 6–8: marketplace review + private offers negotiation (if needed)

11) Open questions / decisions (short list)
- Do we support marketplace metering APIs for hosted API purchases or limit to private offers for all paid purchases? (impact: finance, metering infra)
- What is our default support SLA for marketplace buyers vs direct enterprise customers?
- What discount/commitment tiers do we permit to be offered via private offer? Who approves the discount?

12) Action items (owners + next steps)
- Jordan: finalize short/long copy + coordinate hero screenshot capture (due 2026-03-07)
- Asha: compile SSO test accounts and SAML docs for Azure (due 2026-03-10)
- Mateo: draft SKU mapping & metering contract template (due 2026-03-14)
- Priya: assemble screenshot pack and one-pager layout (due 2026-03-12)
- Samir: request SOC2 redacted package and confirm support SLAs with Security & Legal (due 2026-03-09)

Notes / scratch (working thoughts)
- Consider shipping AWS SaaS listing first with metering for small customers to validate purchase flow, but gate larger Dedicated offerings behind private offers to preserve margin.
- Keep listing copy consistent across marketplaces but adapt to the UI constraints (character limits).
- Track marketplace fees in pricing model and show example TCO comparison in GTM enablement deck.

End of draft — add comments inline or update checklist statuses as items are completed.
